chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Al-Nawfali, from Al-Sakuni, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

When the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) ate at the home of a family, he would say to them: 'The fasting ones have eaten with you, and the righteous have eaten with you, and the chosen angels have sent blessings upon you.'
ai.seo_question: What is the supplication the Prophet said when eating at someone's house?
ai.summary: In al-Kafi, Shaykh al-Kulayni records this supplication as a model of prophetic etiquette, where the Prophet (peace be upon him) transforms a simple meal into a spiritual event by invoking the presence of fasting believers, the righteous, and the chosen angels. This practice underscores the Shia emphasis on the sanctity of hospitality, linking material generosity with divine blessing (barakah) and communal solidarity. It serves as a practical guide for Muslims to elevate everyday acts of hosting into acts of worship through mindful invocation.
